notes: Windows bootstrap must not depend on Python in order to discover and record Python runtime availability.
All successful discovery paths are rebound to the resolved interpreter executable; later governed stages do not execute through py.exe, PATH python shims, or uv run.

If no existing Python 3.11+ interpreter executes and uv itself is available, bootstrap may provision CPython into the repository-local .runtime/python directory. This bounded repair does not modify system PATH and is excluded from source control.
uv locator and install behavior follows uv's documented Python discovery/install interfaces. Provider acquisition remains forbidden until the resolved interpreter executes successfully.
WSL is intentionally not used as an automatic fallback because Windows-path and filesystem semantics would change the governed runtime boundary.
On Windows, bootstrap.cmd and run_python.cmd are the canonical external entrypoints; they apply process-scoped PowerShell ExecutionPolicy Bypass without changing machine policy.
